subject.title: [Feature]: `openclaw backup`: support manifest-backed intentional omissions for protected or reconstructable runtime paths

question: Should the core backup CLI accept operator-declared omissions, and what public input contract should own those rules without weakening the shipped fail-closed default?
rationale: The choice creates a security-sensitive CLI and manifest contract affecting backup completeness, compatibility, and restore expectations; repository evidence cannot choose that permanent policy on maintainer behalf.

options.title: Versioned omission plan
options.body: Add an explicit `--omissions-from <json>`-style plan using exact anchored paths first, with classified manifest entries and strict verification.

options.title: Built-in rules only
options.body: Expand only OpenClaw-owned volatile and reconstructable rules in code, avoiding operator policy but leaving service-owned deployment paths unsupported.

options.title: Keep strict behavior
options.body: Retain unconditional failure and document external backup tooling for deployments with protected subtrees.

recommendation.title: Versioned omission plan
recommendation.body: Add an explicit `--omissions-from <json>`-style plan using exact anchored paths first, with classified manifest entries and strict verification.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed, hardened, and merged the existing backup public contract and are the strongest available routing candidate for its next security-sensitive API decision.
